newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-SELES MAKES WINNING START AT ITALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES MAKES WINNING START AT ITALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Top seed Monica Seles and fellow American Jennifer Capriati made contrasting returns to the Italian Open on Tuesday after long absences, the former winning easily and the latter losing in disarray.

Seles, playing at the Foro Italico for the first time for five years, encountered some stiff opposition from Austrian Barbara Schett in the first set of her second round match but moved up a level to win through 7-5 6-0.
Capriati, back at the clay tournament after four years, lost 7-6 6-2 in the first round to compatriot Chanda Rubin.
The former teen prodigy should have wrapped up the first set when she had three set points at 5-3.
Instead, she let the determined Rubin, ranked one place below her at 29th in the world, back into the match with repeated double faults and poor service returns.
Seles also faltered in the first set when, with three set points on her serve at 5-4, she was unable to prevent 21-year-old Schett from coming back and then breaking her serve.
The Austrian was unable to keep up the pressure and handed Seles the set with a double fault on her serve.
The second set was a procession with the late-night match wrapped up on the hour.
"It was great to be playing back in front of the crowd in Rome after five years," Seles said.
"I played really well in the second set...It was tough starting as late as we did and it was pretty cold."

Rain had delayed the start of the match with seventh-seeded Romanian Irina Spirlea's earlier match against Spain's Cristina Torres Valero halted twice. Spirlea edged through 7-5 7-6 and 7-5 on the tiebreak.
Capriati was the biggest disappointment for the crowd of a few hundred hardy spectators on a gusty day.
She was joined in defeat by France's Nathalie Tauziat, the 15th seed and first to fall in the tournament. She lost in three sets to Belgium's Dominique Van Roost in the second round.

Capriati, whose last appearance was before the teenage burnout in 1993 that led to her facing charges of drugs possession and shoplifting, put a brave face on her exit but she had only herself to blame.
"I think that I just really lost my concentration," she said. "I think it was just a bad day for me."
Rubin ran up a 5-1 lead in the second set with Capriati double-faulting twice in the second game and then on break point in the fourth as her opponent forged 4-0 ahead.
Capriati broke back in the fifth, but needed seven attempts to get there, before Rubin broke straight back in a love game. Capriati then broke her again to 5-2.
She then double-faulted in the final game to give Rubin break point and went out with a return to the net.
"She didn't serve very well," said Rubin. "She made a lot more errors than I thought she would."
Rubin now meets champion Conchita Martinez of Spain, the third seed and winner here for the past four seasons. She had a bye into the second round.
